Table C's named PE-5 case: old ALLOWS ~/.claude/hooks/guards/commander.py (still just a .py to a .ps1-only matcher); new BLOCKS it.

M-2/PE-5 table's logs/old.ps1 example: recursion is PRESERVED, not new -- PowerShell's -like '*' already crossed directory separators, so the master ALSO blocks this .ps1 under logs/, proving M-2 rather than PE-5. PE-10 deploy row: old text says 'powershell -File <skill>/hooks/install.ps1'; new says '{python_exe} .../install.py'. The .ps1 installer is not the deploy path any more, so pointing at it would tell the model to run a command that no longer deploys the .py runtime.

PE-13 (owner-approved F-7, ruled on after round1): deploy-guard.ps1 checked no NAMES at all, only the .ps1 extension, so old ALLOWS a direct Write to the deployed config.json. new BLOCKS it via guarded_names -- the deployed config.json is a derived artifact now, and editing it directly reproduces the exact master/deploy drift this guard exists to prevent. Deliberate tightening, same class as PE-5.

The other direction of PE-13's row, so it proves something: guarded_names is scoped to files UNDER deploy_dir, not a blanket ban on the name config.json anywhere. A project's own config.json outside the deployed hooks tree is untouched by this guard, on both old and new sides -- not a divergence, hence parity:true (kept beside the PE-13 case rather than folded into deploy-06 so the pair reads together).
